main_body: Round stone well body (rim, dark water opening and block-built front wall) under a small wooden roof beam on two posts
top_band: Pale grey-green stone rim, rows ~14-16 at the back, wrapping an elliptical dark-blue water opening (rows ~16-21), with a front rim lip at row ~21
evidence: In the middle column the rim is light grey (rows 14-16), then an elliptical dark-blue opening with highlights (rows 16-20), then a lighter front rim line (row ~21), then the front wall of shaded stone blocks (rows 22-31). The opening reads as a real ellipse seen from above, with the front wall below it. No isometric side face. The stone blocks are painted rather than inset, but the construction is correct 3/4.

style.evidence: The stone well has about 5 grey-green steps, a tinted dark outline and shaded block faces with a bit of water glint, which is decent. The wooden roof beam and the posts are large flat tan fills with only a highlight row and a shadow row, and no grain. Several stone blocks are also smooth flat patches. The reference well has richer tile and wood texture, so tiles here carry fewer colours and look thinner next to it.
